children: , the jet-engine and aviation-systems manufacturer, started shipping GE9X engines with a redesigned mid-seal in the third quarter, pushing a key hardware fix into production while the Boeing 777X certification effort continues. Shares slipped roughly 0.3% to $312.46 Friday morning. At that price, GE trades 15.21% above its $271.21 GF Value, showing investors are already paying a meaningful premium for the aerospace recovery story.

The change follows internal testing aimed at a durability issue identified earlier this year, according to Chief Financial Officer Rahul Ghai. The existing seal remains usable for current aircraft-certification work, which gives GE room to keep the broader program moving. The redesigned production seal still needs separate Federal Aviation Administration approval, with management expecting that process to conclude within several months. GE says the issue should not delay the 777X's entry into service.

That distinction matters. GE has effectively kept one component's regulatory clock from becoming the entire aircraft program's clock. But the next phase is about execution, not reassurance: the company still needs final authorization, any necessary hardware retrofits and consistent production quality as deliveries ramp. With the stock already sitting above GF Value, investors will be looking for clean regulatory completion and on-time engine deliveries to justify that premium.

title: GE Aerospace Slips as GE9X Fix Enters Certification
